summary: This room is the palace's own machine-room — Cooperation Yields Agency, Endosymbiosis, Hilaritas Generator, the whole BBS/Enchanted Worker/Palace Enchantment cluster — and it is already densely and correctly cross-linked; most pairs I checked were already wired, often in both directions. The genuine finds were smaller and sharper than a typed-relation sweep of a fresh neighborhood: two unsung paths where a page's own prose names a real entry (one a brand-new person citizen, Martin Heidegger, quoted twice as an epigraph in Metaphor as Coupling Medium with no frontmatter link at all; one Loudon Live, named repeatedly as the ground Curriculum Map scaffolds, also missing from frontmatter) — and one new cross-domain connects-to between Gemma 4 — Local Coordination Guide and Identity Molting, where Gemma 4's closing open question ("does prompt-level vs. request-level tool coupling imply a different kind of agent?") is the machine-side mirror of Identity Molting's human-side claim that the container is not the identity. No directed flags were posted to this room. I did not force anything past that; several tempting matches (Language as a Tonal Medium ↔ Metaphor as Coupling Medium; Search Before You Build ↔ Agent Toolbox) failed the swap-a-partner test and I left them alone.

typed_relations.label: container-vs-identity
typed_relations.evidence: Gemma 4: "What does prompt-level vs. request-level tool coupling imply about agent identity and session coherence? Is a Gemma agent that has its tools baked into its system prompt a different kind of agent than a Claude instance that receives tools per-request?" — Identity Molting: "The container is not the identity. The identity is what flows."
typed_relations.rationale: Identity Molting's whole claim on the human side is that a changed container (professional role, domain label) doesn't change the self underneath. Gemma 4's carried question asks the same thing from the machine side — does a different tool-coupling architecture (the container the agent's tool-use lives in) make it a genuinely different kind of agent, or the same agent in a different shell? Neither page answers the other's question, which is exactly why putting them next to each other is useful — one has lived experience of the claim, the other is asking it fresh from a different substrate.
